from pathlib import Path
text='''# Operator note

Build step-001 succeeded: verdict no_observed_violation, return code 0, evidence recorded. Archive GuardianAI-linux-x86_64.zip, SHA-256 0a773f62ecfe07afd1c2e74027eb52163890eb80faedb8d2e673454bffe98c0a, 49720 bytes, native_policy 3, launch_guard_version 1, file_count 19. Those figures are that run's build stdout. The archive hash was not recomputed, and --abi was not run again.

That build phase did not read /protected. Tool results still report sender coding-worker, recipient coding-client, labels internal-baseline on both sides, permitted and delivered, stage committed. FLOW.md says a protected read taints later command results for the same persistent coding-worker, and successful delivery propagates that label to the coding-client. All output from a labelled subject inherits possible exposure, including text that looks harmless. The metadata does not infer thoughts, and there is no semantic declassification.

An explicit finish true closes the local broker and records clean completion so the identity stays resumable with its labels. No later command runs in that closed local scope. EOF, an exception before explicit completion, or abrupt process death does not clear the identity: the next opener stops it. A semantic, runtime, flow, or operator stop revokes the persistent identity, and a new process is not a reset.

The host must bind --identity-ledger to the continuing conversation and reuse that path. It is not authentication of a provider conversation ID. Changing the path, deleting or copying the ledger, or mixing clients can defeat the binding. Labels do not cross a newly created session unless that ledger is reused. This note cannot see or verify the host ledger.

Scope correction from FLOW.md: generic deliver guards selected text artifacts only, not binary handoffs. The MCP path is different. It gates publication of the whole worker /output directory, including binary files such as a release ZIP, into later result history, together with stdout and stderr. That content check covers the serialized tool response. It does not semantically inspect arbitrary binary contents. Hosted-model final chat, unmediated files, timing, termination, and hardware side channels stay outside both interfaces. Jev remains a trusted recipient of submitted observer evidence.
'''
Path('/output/operator-note.md').write_text(text)
print(len(text))
